subject: End-of-commitment notification exceptions & sunset runbook — MSA/Order Form redlines

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: End-of-commitment notification exceptions & sunset runbook — MSA/Order Form redlines

Hi Linda —

Thanks again for the conversation this week. Per our call, attached is a proposed set of redlines that try to balance ACME's need for an orderly sunsetting path with Redwood's platform economics. Key points for your review:

- Auto-renew: we left the standard 12-month auto-renew but added a mutual-exception carveout for pilots and short-term proof-of-value deals (Section 2.1 exception).
- Notice window: proposed mutual 60-day written notice; alternative staggered approach in the attached transition matrix if you need more runway for specific teams.
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): proposed limited TFC language that preserves customer rights but caps transition liability to a defined transition fee (3 months of committed spend) and includes a data export SLA.

Attachments: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx, ~210KB), sunset_transition_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, ~85KB)

Request: can you loop in ACME legal and procurement comments inline on the docx? If helpful we can do a short call to walk the proposed language and the runbook.

Next step suggestion: procurement + legal review by EOD Thu; redraw and then final legal sync next week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: End-of-commitment notification exceptions & sunset runbook — MSA/Order Form redlines

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. I added ACME Legal on this thread (legal@acme.com). A couple of quick clarifying questions before legal does a line-by-line:

1) Can you confirm whether the 60-day mutual notice is calendar days or business days? Procurement prefers business days for operational clarity.
2) For the TFC cap: does the 3-month cap include any unbilled committed capacity or only recurring subscription fees?
3) On data export SLA — can you outline expected formats, retention timeline post-termination, and whether we can request a one-time extended access window for exports?

We will do an internal procurement + legal readout tomorrow morning and send consolidated line items. If Redwood can provide a short rider that lists the exact Order Form fields that will change on signature that would speed our legal review.

Thanks,
Linda Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager — ACME Corp
procurement@acme.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-11T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-of-commitment notification exceptions & sunset runbook — MSA/Order Form redlines

Thanks Linda — quick reply from the sales side to clarify intent and options so legal has context.

High level approach we recommend:
- Notice window: default to 60 business days (we're flexible on calendar vs business; 60 business days effectively equals ~3 months and gives ops predictable runway).
- TFC cap: the 3-month figure is intended to cover committed subscription fees only (not retrospective credits or unbilled special discounts). We can make it explicit: "three (3) months of recurring subscription fees as set forth in the Order Form."
- Data export: Redwood will provide a one-time export in JSON/CSV for user-level data plus a bulk backup in Parquet on request; standard retention is 30 days post-termination with an option to extend to 90 days for an agreed fee (we've captured the optional extended access in the transition matrix).

I've attached an operational transition matrix that maps teams, export owners, and estimated transfer windows so legal/procurement can see how the 60-day window is intended to be used operationally.

Attachments: sunset_transition_matrix.xlsx

If ACME legal wants to propose exact track-changes on the docx, we're good to respond the same day. Otherwise, propose a 30-minute legal alignment call tomorrow at 11am PT.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

On Fri, Jun 11, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Linda —
> 
> Thanks again for the conversation this week. Per our call, attached is a proposed set of redlines...

Jordan / Ben —

We reviewed ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx and left inline comments. A few substantive items:

- Section 2.1 (Auto-renew): request explicit call-out that any pilot contract under $25k is exempt from auto-renew and requires affirmative written extension.
- Notice window: propose 90 calendar days rather than 60 business days to avoid ambiguity across global teams.
- TFC: we accept a capped TFC but request the ability to offset a portion of the fee if Redwood provides migration assistance beyond standard handoff (i.e., if Redwood provides >40 hours of migration support, reduce fee by pro-rated amount).
- Data export: require a certified export log (time-stamped manifest) and a 60-day post-termination access window for critical backups, not just a one-time export.

Attached: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (with track changes). We'll aim to return a clean redline by EOD. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the 90-calendar-day notice and the offset mechanism on TFC.

Regards,
Tom Reed
Senior Counsel — ACME Corp
Tom.Reed@acme.com

Subject: Re: End-of-commitment notification exceptions & sunset runbook — MSA/Order Form redlines

Tom/Linda —

Thanks for the clear comments and the tracked version, Tom. Quick summary of where Redwood can land and proposed next actions:

Agreed points (subject to final wording):
- Pilot carveout: agree to explicit exemption for pilots under $25k. We'll add a sentence to Section 2.1.
- TFC: maintain a capped TFC equal to three (3) months of recurring subscription fees as stated on the Order Form; Redwood accepts an offset mechanism tied to documented migration assistance hours (details to be defined in the sunset runbook).
- Data export: agree to provide a certified export manifest and extend the standard access window to 60 days for critical backups. We'll include export format options (JSON/CSV/Parquet) in the runbook.
- Notice window: we can accept 90 calendar days in lieu of 60 business days to simplify cross-region coordination.

Next steps:
1) Redwood legal will incorporate ACME's tracked comments into the attached docx and return a revised clean redline by EOD Monday.
2) Marissa Cole (copied) will own the final Order Form updates and coordinate DocuSign routing once legal confirms language.
3) Ben will schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough with ACME ops to validate the transition matrix assumptions.

For traceability I'm also adding the HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4567 and we'll share a DocuSign envelope once the final redline is agreed: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123

If that sounds good I suggest we lock the final language Monday and target signature the following week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
